tasks.short: Coordinate production staff and partners to turn approved promotional plans into finished materials.

steps.what: Assemble production requirements from the approved campaign brief in the {DOCS}.
Discuss feasibility, dependencies and creative requirements with production staff.
Agree the production approach, delivery dates and responsibilities.
Enter owners, deadlines and dependencies in the {PROJECT}.
Chase routine production updates through the {EMAIL}.
Review production proofs against the brief and request corrections.

loop.input: Production proof, production brief, brand guidelines and approved claim register.
loop.output: Draft discrepancy list with proof locations and supporting references.
loop.check: Rules check dimensions, required wording and dates; a person judges message, imagery and claims.
loop.stop: One assessment and one correction pass per proof; unreadable or ambiguous material goes to manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rules catch fixed requirements but cannot reliably compare meaning across varied copy and layouts.

steps.what: Approve final materials and authorize their handoff to the production partner.

tasks.design: A template generator assembles the production brief from approved fields in the {DOCS}, and configured rules in the {PROJECT} create tasks and surface blockers. A bounded proof checker drafts discrepancies against approved requirements; people resolve creative trade-offs and authorize the final partner handoff.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements arrived in different document formats. Teams relied on conversations and mailbox follow-up to keep production aligned.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing task rules handle routing and deadlines. AI-assisted coding makes a small template generator and proof-checking connector cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Creative quality, changing specifications and partner capacity remain judgement calls. Reliable checks on complex visual proofs can be expensive.
tasks.human_edge: Translate creative intent into feasible production choices and resolve disagreements without losing the message.

ambition.what: Weekly production risk review across active campaigns

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time assembling packs and chasing updates, and more time resolving production risks. Formal budget and release approval rights do not change.

reach.learn: File specifications, accessibility requirements and how layout changes affect meaning.

reach.task: Prioritize production changes across concurrent campaigns.
reach.learn: Capacity planning and the cost of late specification changes.

evidence.claim: Rule-based style checks can support repeatable quality gates; they do not establish creative quality.
Task routing, template assembly and shared status records are established deterministic patterns.
The proposed effort and remaining-time estimates are design assumptions, not measured outcomes.

assumptions: A shared {PROJECT} holds production tasks, while the {EMAIL} still carries follow-up and approvals.
Approved campaign fields and claim references can be maintained in the {DOCS}.
Routine chasing disappears only if production staff update the shared board; exception conversations remain.
Build ranges cover a first usable workflow and can overlap with other tasks.
GDPR applies to personal data. Access review includes employee consultation under national rules where required.
unknowns: Which proof formats, task rules and connectors are available?
Who may approve production changes and partner handoffs?
Do production partners use the shared board?
Which national rules and existing employee agreements apply?
research_questions: Which proof defects can be checked reliably without interpreting imagery?
Does the shared board remove routine chasing during a live campaign pilot?
new_work: Review generated production briefs for missing requirements.
Resolve proof-checker false positives and unreadable files.
Maintain task templates, claim references and connector permissions.
Handle overdue dependencies and partners who do not update shared records.

tasks.short: Work with agencies and internal staff to agree promotional campaigns, spending and delivery plans.

steps.what: Discuss campaign objectives, audiences and constraints with the marketing manager.
Write the agency brief in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Confirmed objectives, constraints, brand guidelines and approved claim register.
loop.output: Draft campaign brief in a fixed template, with unresolved questions marked.
loop.check: Required-field validation, source references and specialist review of audience and message choices.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing objectives or unsupported claims return to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle structure, but turning contextual objectives into clear agency instructions needs language synthesis.

steps.what: Send the brief and clarify proposal requirements with the agency.
Compare agency proposals, fees, deliverables and exclusions in a {SPREADSHEET}.

loop.input: Agency proposals and a fixed comparison schema.
loop.output: Source-linked fee, deliverable, timing and exclusion fields.
loop.check: Code checks totals, currencies and missing fields; the specialist checks scope equivalence.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per proposal; unclear fees or exclusions remain explicitly unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: Proposals express scope and exclusions in inconsistent prose, although calculations are deterministic.

steps.what: Negotiate campaign approach, deliverables, timing and commercial trade-offs with the agency.
Approve campaign scope and spending through the {PROCUREMENT}.
Enter approved campaign milestones and production requests in the {PROJECT}.

tasks.design: A brief generator in the {DOCS} combines confirmed campaign fields with a bounded drafting loop, while a proposal extractor fills a comparison table in the {SPREADSHEET}. Existing approval rules in the {PROCUREMENT} control spending, and the approved scope creates milestones in the {PROJECT}; agency negotiation stays with people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agency proposals used different scope descriptions and fee structures. Decisions depended on relationships and trade-offs that a campaign form could not settle.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded extraction can normalize proposal prose while code checks arithmetic and completeness. Small connectors can reuse existing approval and task features.
tasks.still_hard: Equivalent-looking proposals may buy different rights, quality or reach. Negotiating value and judging channel fit remain difficult.
tasks.human_edge: Judge whether an agency understands the audience and negotiate a workable campaign without weakening its purpose.

ambition.what: Fortnightly channel reallocation review using comparable campaign plans

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends more of the week testing campaign choices and negotiating scope, with less brief assembly and proposal copying. Spending and contractual approval rights stay with designated approvers.

reach.learn: Incremental reach, attribution limits and contractual cancellation costs.

reach.role: Market Research Analysts and Marketing Specialists
reach.task: Challenge the audience assumptions in an agency proposal.
reach.learn: Sampling limits, audience evidence and how to frame a testable campaign hypothesis.

evidence.claim: A controlled study found productivity and quality gains on professional writing tasks; it did not test agency negotiation.
Repeatable style checks can support review of generated briefs.
Proposal extraction, arithmetic checks and approval routing are a proposed combination, without a documented end-to-end case here.

assumptions: The specialist coordinates agencies but does not independently commit campaign spending.
A {SPREADSHEET} bridges proposal documents because agency scope is not standardized.
The first release covers brief drafting and comparison, not automated media buying.
GDPR applies to audience and contact data; employee consultation follows national rules where applicable.
Build ranges assume existing approval features can be configured.
unknowns: What are the actual spending limits and contract approval roles?
Can agency proposals be processed under existing confidentiality agreements?
Which campaign fields and procurement interfaces are available?
Are audience inputs aggregated or personally identifiable?
research_questions: Which comparison fields prevent the most consequential scope misunderstandings?
Can the pilot preserve exclusions and usage rights across varied proposal formats?
new_work: Review generated briefs and unresolved questions.
Check extracted exclusions, fees and usage rights against proposals.
Maintain comparison fields and approval thresholds.
Investigate failed transfers between the {PROCUREMENT} and the {PROJECT}.

tasks.short: Prepare and deliver speeches that explain the organization's position and build public trust.

steps.what: Discuss the audience, occasion and intended message with the speaker.
Gather approved facts, quotations and earlier statements from the {DOCS}.
Draft the speech and speaker notes in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Speech brief, approved source pack and speaker style preferences.
loop.output: Speech draft and notes with source references for claims and exact quotations.
loop.check: Rules validate quotation matches, source identifiers and estimated length; the specialist reviews meaning and voice.
loop.stop: One draft and two revisions; unsupported claims become questions, and invented anecdotes or quotations are rejected.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template cannot produce a coherent spoken narrative suited to the occasion and speaker.

steps.what: Verify technical claims and clear sensitive factual passages.
Revise personal wording and approve the speech script.
Rehearse delivery, timing and likely audience questions with the speaker.
Deliver the speech and respond to the audience.

tasks.design: A deterministic source-pack generator retrieves approved, tagged material from the {DOCS}, then a bounded drafting loop produces a referenced script and speaker notes. Fixed checks catch unmatched quotations and missing references; subject experts and the speaker clear the script, rehearse and deliver it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Source material was scattered, and each speaker needed a distinct voice. Earlier automation could format notes but could not draft a useful narrative.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded drafting can work from a small approved source pack. Source identifiers, exact quotation checks and existing document versioning constrain the output.
tasks.still_hard: Authenticity, emotional timing and live audience response stay human. Source matching cannot establish that a claim remains true or appropriate.
tasks.human_edge: Choose what the speaker can credibly say and adapt to the audience in the room.

ambition.what: Source-backed audience question rehearsal for occasional speakers

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time finding approved material and drafting routine passages, freeing time for rehearsal and audience preparation. The speaker retains responsibility for the words and live delivery.

reach.task: Develop the narrative arc of a speech.
reach.learn: Spoken rhythm, transitions and ethical use of personal stories.

reach.task: Plan speaker timing and audience participation.
reach.learn: Run-of-show planning, accessibility and room constraints.

evidence.claim: A controlled professional-writing study supports potential drafting gains, but does not establish gains in live speech delivery.
Spelling, grammar and style checks are available as existing capabilities.
The digest documents a publishing failure involving invented quotations, supporting exact quotation checks and human review.
Source-pack assembly and speech-specific remaining-time estimates are proposed design assumptions.

assumptions: The task covers a prepared speech with rehearsal; spontaneous speaking would have a different time split.
The speaker may be the specialist or another authorized representative.
Automatic source-pack assembly uses approved tags and registers; it does not discover or validate new facts.
No synthetic voice or likeness is needed.
GDPR applies to personal stories and speaker data. AI transparency obligations should be assessed for the actual publication format.
unknowns: Who usually delivers speeches and who clears sensitive claims?
Does an approved claim and quotation register exist?
Are speeches published, recorded or translated?
Which source material is licensed and permitted for model processing?
research_questions: Can speakers use the generated drafts with fewer structural rewrites?
Do source references remain intact through document revisions and final approval?
new_work: Maintain approved facts, quotations and expiry dates.
Review generated wording for authenticity and unsupported implications.
Recheck factual changes made after expert clearance.
Maintain drafting instructions and source-reference validation.

tasks.short: Coordinate verified, approved public communication during environmental incidents and conflicts.

steps.what: Read incident alerts and record immediate communication questions from the {EMAIL}.

loop.input: Incident alert and attachments permitted for processing.
loop.output: Source-linked intake notes separating reported facts, uncertainties and communication questions.
loop.check: Required fields and source links are checked; the specialist confirms urgency and missing information.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair; conflicting or unreadable alerts go directly to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Alerts arrive as inconsistent prose and may mix observations, assumptions and requests.

steps.what: Verify the incident facts and uncertainties with operations and environmental specialists.
Decide response priorities, spokesperson and communication timing.
Draft a holding statement and response questions in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Confirmed communication mandate, verified facts, uncertainty log and previous statements.
loop.output: Referenced holding statement and question responses that preserve uncertainties.
loop.check: Rules flag unsupported numbers, names and commitments; the specialist reviews tone and factual implications.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per fact version; missing clearance or contradictory facts halt drafting for escalation.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates supply structure but cannot express a specific incident clearly without contextual language synthesis.

steps.what: Check environmental claims and clear technical wording.
Approve exact statement wording, channels and release timing.
Publish the authorized statement through the {CMS} and the {SOCIAL}.
Monitor public reactions and brief the incident lead on emerging concerns.

loop.input: Licensed media mentions and public questions within configured incident filters.
loop.output: Source-linked concern groups, unanswered questions and suggested escalations.
loop.check: The specialist reviews escalations and a sample of excluded items; urgent keyword rules alert independently.
loop.stop: One classification pass per item and a fixed batch limit; overflow or uncertain urgency routes to manual triage.
loop.why_not_simpler: Keywords handle known incident terms but miss paraphrased concerns and context-dependent questions.

tasks.design: The {WORKFLOW} holds a versioned incident record, approvals and response deadlines, while bounded loops draft intake notes and statements from verified material in the {DOCS}. Configured publishing in the {CMS} and the {SOCIAL} requires authorization tied to the exact text, channels and timing; monitoring groups concerns for human escalation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Facts changed quickly across operations, specialists and communications. Email approvals could become detached from the statement version actually released.
tasks.enabler_now: Versioned approvals and publication rules are established capabilities. Bounded extraction and drafting reduce paperwork without delegating fact verification or incident command.
tasks.still_hard: Environmental harm, public fear and legal duties cannot be resolved from text alone. Outages, disputed facts and fast-changing conditions require practiced human coordination.
tasks.human_edge: Acknowledge uncertainty honestly, listen to affected people and coordinate commitments that operations can fulfil.

ambition.what: Affected-community question register with accountable response deadlines

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time consolidating alerts and copying approved text, and more time listening to affected groups and resolving unanswered questions. Incident command, technical clearance and public release authority remain explicitly assigned.

reach.task: Explain the evidence and limits behind environmental impact statements.
reach.learn: Measurement uncertainty, environmental terminology and the distinction between observations and projections.

reach.task: Recommend escalation and the next public update.
reach.learn: Incident command, stakeholder mapping and how to set credible update commitments.

evidence.claim: Conversation and news monitoring, plus scheduled posting, are available capabilities.
Claim detection and repeat matching can support triage but do not verify incident facts.
A documented study found substantial issues in AI-generated news answers, supporting source-bound drafts and human factual clearance.
Public-interest AI-generated text has transparency requirements with an editorial-review exception described in Article 50.
The incident workflow, build ranges and remaining-time estimates are proposed design assumptions.

assumptions: An incident lead and environmental specialist already have defined responsibilities.
The workflow supports public communication; statutory reporting and emergency response remain separate duties.
Publication uses the approval recorded in step s6, without a duplicate approval meeting.
Any text, channel or timing change invalidates the release authorization; failed publication escalates without model rewriting.
GDPR applies to incident records and public questions; PR has no blanket journalistic exemption.
EU AI Act transparency requirements need assessment for the actual output and editorial process.
Access work includes national employee-consultation requirements where monitoring or working practices trigger them.
Testing includes an incident exercise and a manual publishing fallback.
unknowns: Who commands incidents and approves technical, legal and public wording?
Which environmental reporting duties apply to the company's activities and locations?
Can the publishing systems enforce version-bound approval and emergency access?
What monitoring licences, retention rules and access restrictions exist?
Which national rules and employee agreements govern the proposed monitoring?
research_questions: Can a simulated fact change reliably invalidate all pending releases?
Which missed public concerns would require immediate escalation?
Can manual communication continue during connector or publishing outages?
new_work: Review intake notes and preserve uncertainty as facts change.
Maintain incident contacts, escalation rules and publication permissions.
Review monitoring exclusions and missed concerns.
Run incident exercises and test the manual fallback.
Audit release versions, failed publications and approval invalidation.
Maintain retention limits and access controls for sensitive incident records.

role.altitude: The role shifts toward audience judgement, creative coordination and trusted public communication. Preparation and handoffs become lighter; spending, technical clearance and public release remain assigned to accountable people.
reach: Advertising and Promotions Managers: compare campaign choices and recommend reallocations.
Graphic Designers: identify production risks before materials are finalized.
Writers and Authors: shape speeches around a credible narrative.
Sustainability Specialists: explain environmental evidence and uncertainty.
skills_to_grow: Write structured briefs with explicit decisions, constraints and source references.
Check claims, quotations and implied commitments.
Read campaign evidence and understand attribution limits.
Negotiate scope and resolve creative disagreements.
Maintain approval rules, exception queues and access controls.
Apply GDPR, relevant EU AI Act obligations and national consultation rules.
role.ambitious_version: Offer an evidence-backed communications readiness service: campaign production checks, speaker question rehearsal and an affected-community question register. Use shared records and bounded drafting to support this service while people retain public judgement and approval.
